hints: A path may begin at any node, not necessarily at the root, so consider sums of downward segments inside a root-to-node path.
Define a prefix sum from the root to the current node. Two prefix sums determine the sum of the segment between them.
If the current prefix is P, look for earlier prefixes equal to P - targetSum.
Because the prefix map represents only the current DFS path, remember to remove the current prefix when backtracking.
title: Path Sum III Problem

notes: A valid path may start at any node and may end at any node below it.
Node values may be negative, so prefix sums cannot rely on monotonicity.
The path direction is always downward from parent to child.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 1000].
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: There are three downward paths whose values sum to 8: 5→3, 5→2→1, and -3→11.
Three downward paths in the tree have a total of 22, including paths that start below the root.

content.problemStatement:
With the `root` of a binary tree and an integer `targetSum`, output *the number of paths where the sum of the values along the path equals* `targetSum`.

The path does not need to start or end at the root or a leaf, but it must go downwards (i.e., traveling only from parent nodes to child nodes).

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/04/09/pathsum3-1-tree.jpg)

```
Input: root = [10,5,-3,3,2,null,11,3,-2,null,1], targetSum = 8
Output: 3
Explanation: The paths that sum to 8 are shown.
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: root = [5,4,8,11,null,13,4,7,2,null,null,5,1], targetSum = 22
Output: 3
```

**Constraints:**

* The number of nodes in the tree is in the range `[0, 1000]`.
* `-10^9 <= Node.val <= 10^9`
* `-1000 <= targetSum <= 1000`

notes: Prefix sums require 64-bit arithmetic because root-to-node sums can exceed 32-bit integer range.
Use 64-bit prefix sums because up to 1000 node values can each have magnitude 10^9.
Backtracking removes a prefix count after both children are processed, preventing paths from mixing nodes from different branches.
solution.approach: Use depth-first search with a running prefix sum and a frequency map of prefix sums on the current root-to-node path. When the current prefix is P, every earlier prefix equal to P - targetSum defines a downward path ending at the current node whose sum is targetSum. Add the current prefix before exploring children and remove it when backtracking so the map contains only prefixes from the current path.

better.complexity: O(nh) time in the worst case and O(h) auxiliary space.
better.description: Run a depth-first traversal while keeping the entire current root-to-node path. For each node, scan backward through the path and count suffixes whose sum equals targetSum. This avoids starting a separate traversal from every node but still scans the path for every node.

optimal.complexity: O(n) expected time and O(h) auxiliary space with hashing.
optimal.description: Maintain the frequency of prefix sums along the current DFS path. If the current prefix is P, then the number of valid paths ending here is the frequency of P - targetSum. Backtrack by decrementing the current prefix before returning to the parent.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n^2) time in the worst case and O(h) auxiliary recursion space.
bruteForce.description: For every node, start a downward traversal from that node and accumulate sums until each descendant. Count a path whenever its running sum equals targetSum. This directly follows the definition but repeats work across many starting nodes.

solution.timeComplexity: O(n) expected time with a hash map, where n is the number of nodes.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(h) auxiliary space for recursion and O(h) for the prefix-frequency map, where h is the tree height.

followUps: How would the solution change if paths were allowed to move both upward and downward?
Can the algorithm be implemented iteratively instead of recursively?
How would you adapt the method if the tree were a general rooted tree rather than a binary tree?

hidden.label: Duplicate target sums in both branches
Target small relative to node values
Irregular tree with deep target path
Several paths reach the same target

learningObjectives: Recognize when prefix sums can transform a path-sum problem into a lookup problem.
Use DFS backtracking to maintain state along a root-to-node path.
Use a hash map to count repeated prefix sums efficiently.
Handle negative values and 64-bit running sums safely.
